mandatoryCriteria: Database-only notification effects and outbox settlement commit atomically; transaction row locks are the single-database consumer fence and crash rollback releases them.
A recoverable job-specific SQL error rolls back that job's partial effects before persisting bounded retry/backoff or terminal quarantine, while an independent valid job can finish.
Required schema/configuration failures still fail closed and retain accepted work; never mark undelivered work delivered.
Concurrent consumers and restart after a rolled-back transaction preserve one logical notification per source/recipient. Real separate PostgreSQL connections prove locking behavior.
Invitation delivery privacy/idempotency and comment redaction/source locks remain intact. External provider exactly-once delivery is not claimed.
Recovering a job savepoint must persist the comment allowlist again; rollback cannot restore a legacy body/recipient copy into a retry or terminal job.
Independent review of the final frozen source is required; these tests do not approve closure.
